llm.summary: The skill's files and scripts match its stated purpose, but its runtime evidence contract requires the agent to read workspace memory notes and emit full snippet text into the transcript and to write/patch AGENTS.md — a real privacy/exposure risk that users should be aware of before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (deterministic retrieval + compression pipeline) align with included assets and scripts: router.yml, compressor prompt, JSON schemas, installer, validator, and watchdog. The requested operations (install spec that copies assets into workspace, validate them, run watchdog against workspace/memory) are coherent for 'applying' a memory pipeline.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md mandates running scripts that read workspace files (memory/always_on.md, memory topics, AGENTS.md) and requires the agent to emit the full Retrieval Bundle JSON (including snippet text and paths) and the Context Pack JSON into the transcript. This is within the skill's stated purpose but forces disclosure of workspace memory contents verbatim — potentially exposing sensitive information. It also requires the agent to modify AGENTS.md and copy files into the repo, which are destructive-capable actions the agent must be allowed to perform.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No remote downloads or package installs: the skill is instruction-heavy and ships its own helper scripts and assets. The provided scripts copy files from the skill's bundled assets into a workspace directory and perform local validation. No external URL fetches or extract-from-arbitrary-URL behavior detected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials, which is proportionate. However, its runtime contract mandates exporting internal memory snippets and file contents into agent transcripts (including snippet text and file paths), which is effectively a required data-exfiltration surface for any sensitive workspace data. No credentials are required, but the required data access is broad.

dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (normal). The skill will write files into workspace/context_pipeline_v1 (via install_pipeline.py) and patch AGENTS.md per its apply flow — writable repository access is required and expected, not hidden. It does not auto-enable itself platform-wide (no always:true).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Before installing or applying this skill, be aware it will: (1) copy the packaged spec files into your repository (context_pipeline_v1/) and patch AGENTS.md, (2) require reading your workspace memory files (memory/always_on.md and memory/topics/*.md) and emit snippet text and IDs into the agent transcript (Retrieval Bundle JSON and Context Pack JSON), and (3) refuse to proceed unless those artifacts are produced (it will return NOT EXECUTED otherwise). Actions to consider: - Review your workspace memory files for any secrets or PII; if present, do not install in that workspace or move sensitive files out of the memory path first. - Run the included scripts locally yourself (install_pipeline.py, validate_pipeline.py, memory_watchdog.py) in a safe/test workspace to inspect outputs before giving the agent permission to run them. - Require manual review of AGENTS.md diffs before committing (do not auto-commit). - If you want similar functionality without exposing raw snippets, modify the runtime checklist/compressor to redact or limit snippet text before emission. - The skill does not fetch remote code or request credentials, which reduces supply-chain risk, but the forced transcript emission of workspace data is the main concern. If you can confirm your memory files contain no sensitive data and you accept the repo-write behavior, the skill appears coherent for its purpose; otherwise treat it as high-risk and run the scripts manually in isolation.
llm.findings: [no_pre_scan_findings] expected: The static pre-scan reported no injection signals. This does not reduce the practical risk from the runtime evidence contract that requires emitting workspace memory contents into the transcript and modifying AGENTS.md.
